script.base: Closed roof, near pick'em: HOU -1.5, total 40.5, implied HOU 21.0 and DEN 19.5. Most likely a competitive, modest-scoring game with no blowout flag, so starter snaps hold. Dobbins keeps the DEN carry load (43/232, 5.4 YPC over weeks 6-8) while HOU splits Chubb 33/133 and Marks 28/101. Nix and Stroud throw enough for primary targets, not a shootout; Engram's short middle routes stay in the script.
script.flip1: HOU gets up early behind a defense that has allowed 4.05 YPC and only 19 passes of 20+ yards (232 yards) in 7 games. DEN trails, Dobbins' carries stall, and Nix's attempts rise toward Franklin (22 targets, 301 air yards L3), Sutton and Engram. HOU finishes on the ground with Chubb.
script.flip2: Dobbins repeats the 5.4 YPC form, DEN leads, and Stroud is forced to throw into DEN's 34% blitz, where HOU is -0.14 EPA/db versus +0.23 with no blitz. Collins, Higgins and Noel deep yards stall; checkdowns to Marks and Schultz rise; Chubb's late carries shrink.

matchup.pressure: HOU blitzes 25%; DEN is better when blitzed (0.28 EPA/db) than not (0.06), so this is not a pressure-forced checkdown game for Denver. DEN blitzes 34%; Houston is worse when blitzed (-0.14 EPA/db) than not (0.23), which kills HOU deep yards and pushes Stroud toward TE/RB checkdowns if the blitz gets home. Pressure rate and time-to-throw are not in the pack.
matchup.bleeds: HOU bleeds the middle (7.43 YPA), not the outside, and has allowed a modest 19 explosives for 232 yards. DEN bleeds the right (7.94) and the middle (7.04), and has allowed 19 explosives for 293 yards, but the 34% blitz is the constraint on Houston's downfield game. Run: HOU 4.05 YPC and 16 runs of 10+ in 7 games (average, not a pushover); DEN 3.83 YPC and only 9 runs of 10+ in 8 games (stingy).
matchup.overlap: Engram is the overlap: 18 targets at 2.8 air yards per target into the only HOU zone that bleeds (middle 7.43). Franklin (13.7 aDOT, 301 air, 127 yards) and Sutton (12.2 aDOT) attack the outside, where HOU is tighter. On the other side Collins would be the Surtain-out overlap into DEN's right-side bleed, but Stroud's negative EPA versus the blitz cuts against a deep-yard over, and Schultz (the blitz checkdown, 19 targets) is questionable.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Engram under 33.5 cashed. Denver only needed field goals, Dobbins and Nix's legs (8/74 rush L3) handled the 19.5 implied total, and Nix threw about 22 times with Franklin's air yards eating the downfield shots that didn't convert. Engram saw four targets and finished 28-33, a replay of the 33-yard game already in the last four. Houston's middle 7.43 came on just 58 attempts and they sat in a shell that took the hooks away, or Huzzie's replacement was irrelevant because the tight end was chipped and stayed in to block Autry/Horton if those ends played. The number was the season median, so a one-yard miss was the base rate, not a surprise.
slip_story: One-game, one-script slip: competitive dome game, attack Houston's middle, not a shootout stack and not a clock-kill stack. Engram over belongs with a stay-close script; it can coexist with Dobbins carries (it already did in weeks 6-8) but must not be paired with a Denver pass-volume under or a total under if this were expanded. Do not add Schultz, Collins, or any TD. House 3-4 leg slips would need other games; this game produced one qualifying leg. No bet placed.
